items.title: Separation properties of an algebraic space imply that any morphism from it is separated
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file spaces-morphisms.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma with six assertions: an algebraic space X that is separated, locally separated or quasi-separated (absolutely, or over S) has the corresponding property as a morphism, and any morphism f : X -> Y over S is then separated, locally separated or quasi-separated (source lines 657-671). The proof derives parts (4), (5) and (6) from the composition statement applied to the structure morphism of X, and parts (1), (2) and (3) from (4), (5) and (6) by viewing X and Y as algebraic spaces over Spec(Z).
